question: How quickly did mammals grow large after the asteroid, and what did plants have to do with it?
answer: Within about a million years, in step with the plants. Fossils from Corral Bluffs, Colorado, show the largest mammals reaching about 6 kg within 100,000 years of the impact and about 50 kg by 700,000 years, roughly when the first legumes appear there. Protein-rich beans seem to have fed the first big mammals.
move: A recovery at the top waits on what recovers at the bottom.
reference: Lyson et al., Exceptional continental record of biotic recovery after the Cretaceous–Paleogene mass extinction, Science, 2019
